content: I’ll trace dyndep loading, depfile edge registration, and dirty-state propagation, then add a focused regression test and the smallest implementation fix that preserves existing scheduling behavior.

The decisive question is whether the depfile-created input is scanned before its dyndep producer is attached, and which dependent closure is invalidated when that attachment occurs. I’ll inspect only those scan/update routines and the adjacent test harness, then patch.

The root cause is supported: input dirtiness is consumed while inputs are still being traversed. A later order-only input can load dyndep, attach a producer to an earlier depfile input, and mark that earlier input dirty after its result was already consumed. The fix is to visit every input first, then evaluate readiness and dirtiness against the fully updated graph.

The patch transaction was rejected because the tool requires a complete read of `src/graph.cc` before replacing that loop; no files were changed. I’ll satisfy that edit precondition, then apply the same cohesive fix and test.

The read precondition remained unsealed because pagination receipts were split. I can avoid a context-free replacement by anchoring the edit to unchanged surrounding statements, preserving the same implementation.

The patch tool treats any update hunk as requiring one complete-read receipt, including insertion-only hunks. I’m obtaining that receipt in bounded ranges in a single inspection rather than relying on the cursor that the runtime invalidates between calls.
